These incentives reduced depreciation expense by $594 million in 2024, substantially all of which reduced cost of sales, and $3.3 billion of the total capital-related incentives recognized in 2024 was classified as a non-cash investing activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose the recognition of investment tax credits under the CHIPS Act as a component of government incentives, but they report different mechanisms and amounts. MU explicitly states it receives a 25% investment tax credit on qualified U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investments, recognizing these credits in receivables or other noncurrent assets as investments are made. INTC details a more complex incentive package under the CHIPS Act, including an advanced manufacturing investment tax credit of $2.6 billion recognized in 2024, which may be refunded in cash. While both leverage the same federal policy for domestic manufacturing, INTC's disclosure quantifies the specific tax credit amount recognized in the period and mentions potential cash refunds, whereas MU describes the general recognition policy based on investment progression.

sentences.text: Beginning in 2023, we receive a 25% investment tax credit on qualified investments in U.S. semiconductor manufacturing under the CHIPS Act.
As qualified investments are made, we recognize investment tax credits in receivables or other noncurrent assets.

▪US federal government pursuant to the CHIPS Act. In September 2024, we were awarded up to $3.0 billion in direct funding for the Secure Enclave program to expand the trusted manufacturing of leading-edge semiconductors for the US government. In November 2024, we signed a Direct Funding Agreement with the US Department of Commerce for the award of $7.9 billion in government incentives. We recognized $1.3 billion of grants, including $253 million of operating grants, in 2024 under the CHIPS Act. Additionally, we recognized an advanced manufacturing investment tax credit of $2.6 billion in 2024 ($845 million in 2023), which may be refunded to us in cash to the extent it exceeds our outstanding income tax liabilities.
